objective: Complete the declared assembly/transport task correctly and efficiently; allocation, local motion and collaboration are Agent choices.
rules: Deliver the three requested source-identity items to each destination board. Station IDs identify inventory and destination orders, not exclusive robot ownership.

Transfers may be direct airborne handovers or safe stable tabletop staging. There are no marked or mandatory intermediate regions, predefined buffer positions, prescribed routes or fixed transfer pairs. The planner chooses whether to wait, stage or hand over. Establish receiving support before releasing an airborne item.

Each final position shows the required color and shape: a square for a cube and a circle for a cylinder, 1.4 times the object width or diameter. These are visual identity cues, not enlarged acceptance tolerances. Slot numbers and source identities disambiguate orders.

L1: release stably at the final board targets. L2 and L3: both flat blades must enter the real blind slots and the item must be released, seated and stable. L2 has a fixed board; L3 has the same three inline sockets on a passive spring-supported z/roll/pitch board. Preserve prior placements and allow gripper opening and withdrawal clearance.

Cubes have 60 mm sides; cylinders have 60 mm diameter and height. Blades initially point up or sideways. Grasp, airborne reorientation, receiving grasp and subsequent insertion must form a feasible continuous sequence. Allocation, routes and independent concurrent work are planner choices; minimize unnecessary cycling, staging and regrasping while maintaining real support and collision clearance.
Only robot actuators and real contacts may affect the live task. No hand welds, object state writes, resets, hidden state tools or runtime physics edits.

spring_board.support: Equivalent central passive z/roll/pitch mechanism; cosmetic coil is not FEA

mechanism.supplies: Tabletop; no pedestals. Plug blades initially up/sideways. First six stock identities are cubes, subsequent identities are cylinders.

transfer.choice: Planner chooses direct airborne handover, safe tabletop staging or waiting; no fixed routes/pairs

# Transport

## Flow

Plan useful concurrent work from shared goals and current observations. Compare
direct airborne handover, stable tabletop staging and waiting by total handling
cost, occupied arms, release clearance and risk; there are no mandatory buffers,
routes or robot pairs. Plan reach and staging against the task's actual support boxes,
not the outer table bounding rectangle. Account for the whole sequence from initial grasp through
reorientation, receiving grasp, insertion, jaw opening and withdrawal. Keep
placed items accessible and reverify affected placements after contact.

## Handovers

For a shared or transferred item, plan the relative motion of both tools, not only
their individual paths, and preserve receiver access and sender withdrawal when
choosing a grasp. Before releasing an airborne item, establish the receiver's
support from allowed RGB and robot feedback: a commanded grasp, `is_grasped`,
measured aperture or TCP motion alone does not prove support. When uncertain,
choose an informative view or a bounded verification action.

## Insertion

Reason about seating from the whole item pose and both blade envelopes; touching a
socket is not insertion. On a spring board, use its current observed orientation,
which changes under contact. After a known failure, reason from the actual scene
before regrasping or transferring.
